from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic", [
            "Algebra handles static shapes and constant speeds perfectly.",
            "But the real world is curvy and constantly changing.",
            "Calculus measures change at a specific, exact moment."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a square (#00FF00) and a car icon (#FFFF00) moving at constant speed. 
        # Label: 'Algebra: Constant'. Change lecture line 1 color to #FFFF00.
        
        line1_color = "#FFFF00"
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "B3")
        
        # Simple car icon using a Triangle as requested by storyboard context
        car1 = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/2).scale(0.2)
        car1.move_to(self.grid["C2"])
        
        label1 = Text("Algebra: Constant", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "A2")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(line1_color),
            Create(square),
            FadeIn(car1),
            Write(label1)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Constant speed movement to grid C5
        self.play(car1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a curve (#00FFFF) with a car icon (#FFFF00) accelerating. 
        # Label: 'Calculus: Changing'. Change lecture line 2 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Create a quadratic curve for accelerating appearance
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.2 * t**2, 0]),
            t_range=[0, 3],
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        # Place the curve in the designated area
        self.place_in_area(curve, "D2", "F5")
        
        label2 = Text("Calculus: Changing", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D2")
        
        car2 = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/2).scale(0.2)
        # Align car2 with start of curve
        car2.move_to(curve.get_start())
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            Create(curve),
            FadeIn(car2),
            Write(label2)
        )
        
        # Acceleration movement along the curve
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(car2, curve),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash a single point on the curve and draw a tangent line (#FF8C00). 
        # Label: 'Instantaneous Speed'. Change lecture line 3 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Select a point on the curve (alpha is proportion 0.0 to 1.0)
        alpha_point = 0.7
        point_on_curve = curve.point_from_proportion(alpha_point)
        dot = Dot(point_on_curve, color="#FF8C00")
        
        # Tangent line at that point
        tangent = TangentLine(curve, alpha=alpha_point, length=2.5, color="#FF8C00")
        
        label3 = Text("Instantaneous Speed", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label3, "F2")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            Flash(dot, color="#FF8C00"),
            Create(dot),
            Create(tangent),
            Write(label3)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex shapes are hard to measure directly.",
            "We can approximate them using many simpler pieces.",
            "As pieces become infinitely small, the approximation becomes exact."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a circle (#00FFFF) with a triangle (#FFFF00) inside it.
        # Change lecture line 1 color to #FFFF00.
        
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(circle, "B2", "E5")
        
        triangle = RegularPolygon(n=3, radius=2, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        triangle.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            Create(circle),
            FadeIn(triangle),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Replace the triangle with a hexagon (#FF8C00) then a dodecagon (#00FF00).
        # Change lecture line 2 color to #FFFF00.
        
        hexagon = RegularPolygon(n=6, radius=2, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        hexagon.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(triangle, hexagon),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        dodecagon = RegularPolygon(n=12, radius=2, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        dodecagon.move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(hexagon, dodecagon)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # As sides increase, polygon color blends into the circle color.
        # Label: 'n -> Infinity'. Change lecture line 3 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Create label
        n_label = MathTex("n \\to \\infty", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "F3")
        
        # Intermediate polygons for smooth-ish transition to simulate "n -> infinity"
        # We use a few steps to keep performance high and follow instructions
        poly_24 = RegularPolygon(n=24, radius=2, color="#00CCFF", fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(circle.get_center())
        poly_48 = RegularPolygon(n=48, radius=2, color="#00EEFF", fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(circle.get_center())
        # The limit is effectively the filled circle matching the perimeter's color
        circle_fill = Circle(radius=2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(circle.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            Write(n_label),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(dodecagon, poly_24), run_time=1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(poly_24, poly_48), run_time=1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(poly_48, circle_fill), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zooming into any smooth curve eventually reveals a line.",
            "This straight line represents the instantaneous rate of change.",
            "On a roller coaster, your direction is a tangent.",
            "We find this by narrowing the gap between points.",
            "This process of finding slopes is called differentiation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define a roller coaster curve (cubic for smooth look)
        curve_func = lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.2 * x
        curve = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Zoom effect: Transition to a nearly straight line at x=0
        # Derivative at x=0: f'(0) = 0.3(0)^2 - 0.2 = -0.2
        # We simulate zoom by replacing with a straight segment
        line_start = self.grid["C2"]
        line_end = self.grid["E5"]
        zoomed_line = Line(start=line_start, end=line_end, color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(curve, zoomed_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        tangent_label = Text("Tangent", font_size=24, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(tangent_label))
        self.play(Flash(tangent_label, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Car icon - small triangle oriented along the line
        angle = np.arctan2(line_end[1] - line_start[1], line_end[0] - line_start[0])
        car = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15)
        car.rotate(angle - PI/2) # Triangle default points UP
        car.move_to(line_start)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        self.play(car.animate.move_to(line_end), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Transition back to curve to show points converging
        curve_context = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-2.5, 2.5], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve_context, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zoomed_line, car, tangent_label),
            FadeIn(curve_context)
        )
        
        # Use ValueTracker for the moving point
        p1_prop = 0.5 # Center of curve
        p2_prop_tracker = ValueTracker(0.8)
        
        dot1 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p1_prop), color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value()), color=WHITE)
        
        # Secant line between the two dots
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            dot1.get_center(), 
            dot2.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            stroke_width=2
        ) if np.linalg.norm(dot1.get_center() - dot2.get_center()) > 0.01 else Vector(direction=RIGHT, color="#FFFF00").move_to(dot1.get_center()).set_length(0.01))
        # Note: Vector is a fallback to avoid zero-length line issues if necessary, 
        # but Line(a, a) is usually okay or just invisible.
        
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2), Create(secant))
        
        # Move dot2 to dot1
        dot2.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(p2_prop_tracker.animate.set_value(p1_prop), run_time=3)
        dot2.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        diff_text = Text("Differentiation", font_size=32, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(diff_text))
        self.play(Flash(diff_text, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching title and lines from storyboard
        title = "Integration: Summing the Infinite"
        lines = [
            "Integration glues tiny, infinite pieces back into a whole.",
            "It calculates the total accumulation over a period.",
            "Visually, this is the area under a curve.",
            "If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...",
            "We find the total volume of water lost."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_RECTS = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_SWEEP = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_BUCKET = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WATER = "#00FFFF"
        LECTURE_ACTIVE = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.15 * x**2 + 0.5, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.8, color=COLOR_RECTS, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(rects))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.001)
        sweep_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 0.001], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
        sweep_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, curve.underlying_function(0)), 
            color=COLOR_SWEEP, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            if x_val > 0.001:
                new_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_val], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
                m.become(new_area)
            
        def update_line(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            m.set_points_as_corners([
                axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
                axes.c2p(x_val, curve.underlying_function(x_val))
            ])

        self.play(FadeOut(rects))
        self.add(sweep_area, sweep_line)
        sweep_area.add_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.add_updater(update_line)
        
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3)
        sweep_area.remove_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.remove_updater(update_line)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        total_area_label = Text("Total Area", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(total_area_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(sweep_area.animate.set_fill(COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.8), Write(total_area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(sweep_area), FadeOut(total_area_label))
        
        bucket_points = [
            [-0.8, 1, 0], [-0.5, -1, 0], [0.5, -1, 0], [0.8, 1, 0]
        ]
        bucket = Polygon(*bucket_points, color=COLOR_BUCKET)
        self.place_in_area(bucket, "B3", "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pool_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=COLOR_WATER).set_stroke(COLOR_WATER, 2)
        self.place_in_area(pool_rect, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pool water
        pool_water = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.01, color=COLOR_WATER, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        pool_water.move_to(pool_rect.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(bucket), Create(pool_rect), FadeIn(pool_water))
        
        drip_start = bucket.get_bottom() + UP*0.2
        drip_end = pool_rect.get_top() + DOWN*0.1
        
        for _ in range(4):
            drip = Dot(radius=0.06, color=COLOR_WATER).move_to(drip_start)
            self.play(drip.animate.move_to(drip_end), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
            self.remove(drip)
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        water_height_tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        pool_water.add_updater(lambda m: m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(0.01, water_height_tracker.get_value()), about_edge=DOWN))
        
        vol_line = Line(pool_rect.get_left(), pool_rect.get_right(), color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.3)
        vol_label = Text("Total Volume", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        vol_label.next_to(vol_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            water_height_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            Create(vol_line),
            Write(vol_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Weather Icon
        weather_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).shift(LEFT*0.1),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.1),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).shift(RIGHT*0.1)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(weather_icon, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.place_at_grid(stock_line, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)

            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Essence of Calculus: The Art of Change and Accumulation
outline.target_audience: High school students and curious beginners

sections.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
sections.content: Introduction to the core philosophy of calculus. Contrast the world of algebra (static shapes and constant speeds) with the real world (curvy shapes and changing speeds). Use the 'Flash' vs. 'The Turtle' analogy to show the need for measuring change at a specific moment.
sections.example: A car speeding up on a highway. Algebra tells you the average speed over an hour, but Calculus tells you the exact speed at the moment you pass a speed camera.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Limits' and the 'Infinitesimal.' Explain how complex problems can be solved by breaking them into infinitely small, simpler pieces. This sets the stage for both derivatives and integrals.
sections.example: Archimedes approximating a circle by fitting a polygon inside it. As the number of sides (n) approaches infinity, the polygon becomes the circle.

sections.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
sections.content: Focus on the 'Derivative.' Visually demonstrate that if you zoom in enough on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'straight line' is the tangent, representing the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: A roller coaster track. At any single point on a steep drop, your 'direction' is a straight arrow (the derivative). We calculate this by making the distance between two points on the track infinitely small.

sections.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
sections.content: Focus on the 'Integral.' Explain it as the reverse of slicing. If differentiation breaks things down, integration glues them back together to find the 'Total.' Represent this graphically as the area under a curve.
sections.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. If you know the 'rate' of the leak at every second (the derivative), integration sums those infinite tiny drips to tell you the total volume lost.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
sections.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
sections.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

sections.title: Calculus in Action: The Modern World
sections.content: Summarize how these two concepts allow us to model everything in motion. From planetary orbits to the spread of a virus, calculus is the 'engine' under the hood of physics and engineering.
sections.example: A SpaceX Falcon 9 landing. Calculus is used to constantly calculate the changing fuel weight and air resistance to adjust the engines at every millisecond for a perfect touchdown.
